description:
Issue summary: During a midday burst window on 2026-03-12 the NovaDocs dedicated pool experienced a gradual but sustained degradation in p50 token latency and end-to-end throughput. Impact: customer reports ~25% drop in sustained throughput for short-stream requests and increased request queuing (spikes of 429 observed). Environment: dedicated pool (cust-dedicated-42), prod-us-east, mixed workload: many short-lived streaming requests with intermittent KV-cache churn.

Observed behavior: p50 drift started ~14:20 UTC, p99 mostly stable but p50 and average throughput fell. Autoscaler did not provision new slots within the short burst window, and some GPUs reached sustained 95-99% utilization while others were underutilized. No cluster-wide outage; effect localized to subset of hosts.

Customer impact and ask: NovaDocs requests investigation and mitigation to avoid recurrence during daily mid-day bursts and asks for a short-term mitigation while engineering provides a long-term fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NovaDocs tenant config (payload: many short streams < 2s inference each; prefix cache miss rate ~30%). 2) Ramp to ~250 concurrent short streams across 30 routes for 5 minutes starting 14:00 UTC. 3) Observe p50 and throughput in Redwood Console per-route dashboard and per-pool GPU allocations. Expected: autoscaler should add slots quickly and maintain p50 baseline. Actual: p50 increases and throughput falls despite high global free capacity in other hosts.
logs_and_metrics: Sample metrics captured 2026-03-12T14:21:54Z: host-gpu-12 util=98%, host-gpu-13 util=22%, host-gpu-14 util=96%; scheduler.queue_length=42 -> 210 over 2m; autoscaler.scale_events=[] (no new allocations); nvme_read_iops host-gpu-12=18k (baseline 2k); sidecar.checkpoint_writer.ops_per_min=120 on host-gpu-12; kernel-errors=0; 429_count_route=/api/v1/generate=37 in 10m. Relevant logs: "2026-03-12T14:20:31Z scheduler: assign_batch failed slot_lock_timeout tenant=novadocs route=/api/v1/generate"; "2026-03-12T14:20:45Z runtime: prefetch eviction storm - kv_cache_evictions=842 in 30s".
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: short-lived, IO-heavy prefetched streams from a single tenant caused localized NVMe saturation and prefetch/kv_cache churn on a small subset of GPUs. That triggered slot fragmentation and serialization: active slots on saturated hosts stalled, while autoscaler did not react because the burst was short-lived and metrics are averaged over 1m windows.

Evidence: 1) NVMe I/O on affected hosts spiked >8x baseline. 2) Sidecar checkpoint_writer task discovered running frequently on the same hosts (noted by ops team) coincident with eviction storms. 3) Host-level heterogeneity: some GPUs were hot while others had spare capacity -> scheduler affinity and slot packing likely concentrated NovaDocs workload onto a small host set. 4) Autoscaler logs show no scale-out due to reliance on 1m CPU/GPU averages; event pattern was sub-1m peaks.

Temporal correlation: checkpoint_writer cron aligns with observed burst windows. We also observed increased kernel-level context switch rates on hot hosts and longer NVLink latencies measured by runtime tracing.

Open questions: - Is NovaDocs client doing aggressive prewarming/prefetch in combination with periodic background checkpoint tasks? - Why did scheduler pack streams onto same hosts (look into recent placement changes in scheduler v2).

Actions taken so far: - Temporarily added a soft placement rule to spread NovaDocs routes across additional hosts in the pool. - Increased autoscaler sensitivity for the pool by lowering the aggregation window to 20s for the next 6 hours. - Blacklisted checkpoint_writer sidecar on 2 affected hosts pending deeper root cause. - Notified NovaDocs CS for tenant-side mitigations (reduce simultaneous prefetch bursts).
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-12T15:05Z: Acknowledged report from NovaDocs; collecting metrics and escalating to SRE. Asked for traffic timeframe and sample request IDs.

SRE (Diego Ramirez) - 2026-03-12T15:22Z: Found NVMe and prefetch eviction spikes on host-gpu-12/14. Suspect IO churn from checkpointing or background writer. Will try soft placement spread and adjust autoscaler window as mitigation.

Customer (NovaDocs, Lina Chen) - 2026-03-12T15:30Z: Confirmed we run periodic small checkpoint writes from our data-sync sidecar every 5 minutes; can we throttle? We saw p50 rise during our sync windows.

Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-12T15:40Z: Applied placement spread and lowered autoscaler aggregation for prod-us-east dedicated pool. Asking customer to validate if behavior improves during next window.

SRE (Diego Ramirez) - 2026-03-12T16:10Z: Early telemetry shows p50 recovering ~60% after spread and autoscaler change; nvme_iops on host-gpu-12 dropped from 18k to ~4k. Continuing monitoring; preparing follow-up plan.
Eng (Maya Singh) - 2026-03-13T09:12Z: Flagging scheduler packing heuristics. Will open a mitigation PR to add load-aware placement constraints to avoid concentrating short-IO bursts on few hosts.
Customer (Lina Chen) - 2026-03-13T11:00Z: After the temporary changes we saw much better throughput during our next checkpoint window. Thanks — would like a longer-term fix.

Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-14T08:45Z: Consolidating plan: short-term mitigations applied; infra team to implement scheduler spread heuristics; product to evaluate autoscaler config defaults for dedicated pools.
resolution:
Workaround: applied soft placement spread for NovaDocs routes, lowered autoscaler aggregation window to 20s for the pool, and temporarily blacklisted heavy checkpoint_writer sidecar on two hosts. Result: p50 improved ~60% towards baseline and 429s stopped.

Long-term plan: 1) Scheduler change to include IO-aware placement to avoid packing high-IO short streams onto few hosts (ENG-6682). 2) Autoscaler enhancement to detect high-frequency short bursts (short-window anomaly detector) and trigger rapid ephemeral scale-outs. 3) Tenant guidance: recommend NovaDocs throttle or jitter their checkpoint sidecar and reduce coordinated prefetch bursts. 4) Add monitoring alerts for disproportionate NVMe I/O per-host in dedicated pools.

Follow-ups: ENG-6682 (scheduler spread PR), INFRA-7021 (autoscaler smoothing changes), Customer success to confirm scheduled follow-up with NovaDocs in 72 hours.
